subtitle: A king, a monk, and the many faces of faith in Gujarat

panels.shot: split composition, half showing a regal court scene, half a quiet Jain temple cloister
panels.action: On one side, Kumarapala stands crowned and armored in a grand Patan hall; on the other, Hemachandra sits cross-legged in simple robes before a Jain image, both figures turning slightly toward each other across the divide.

dialogue.text: In 12th-century Gujarat, King Kumarapala is praised as Shiva’s devotee, yet Jain monks call him their greatest son; was this a conversion, a compromise, or a new way of ruling?

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी के गुजरात में कुमारपाल शिवभक्त भी कहलाते हैं, पर जैन मुनि उन्हें अपना महान बेटा; ये बदलाव था, समझौता, या राज का नया अंदाज़?

panels.shot: wide aerial view of Patan city and palace complex at dusk
panels.action: The fortified city of Patan spreads under a fading sky, its palace rising above crowded streets and temple spires, as Kumarapala stands on a terrace, gazing over his Solanki capital.

dialogue.text: Around 1143 CE, Kumarapala, of the Chaulukya line, sits on Gujarat’s throne in Patan, ruling a realm that stretches from Saurashtra to Malwa, where many gods share the skyline.

i18n.hi: लगभग ११४३ में चालुक्य वंश के कुमारपाल पाटण के सिंहासन पर, सौराष्ट्र से मालवा तक फैले राज्य में बैठते हैं, जहाँ कई देवता एक ही आसमान बाँटते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a royal temple, pillars framing a Shiva linga
panels.action: Kumarapala, bareheaded, stands solemnly before a polished Shiva linga in a torchlit shrine, priests and courtiers behind him in respectful silence.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions from Veraval, near Somnath, praise him as foremost among Shiva-worshipping kings, remembering his works at that ancient coastal shrine.

i18n.hi: सोमनाथ के पास वेरावल की लिखावटें उन्हें शिवभक्त राजाओं में सर्वोपरि कहती हैं, उस प्राचीन समुद्री मंदिर पर उनके कामों को याद करती हैं।

panels.shot: interior court scene, low-angle wide shot of a plural court
panels.action: In a high-pillared audience hall at Patan, Kumarapala sits on a low throne as Brahmin scholars, Jain monks, and court officials in varied dress stand in ordered rows before him.

dialogue.text: His court, however, is not a single faith’s stage: Brahmin pandits debate, Jain acharyas advise, and merchants whose fortunes span deserts and seas whisper of taxes and trade.

i18n.hi: पर उनका दरबार किसी एक मजहब का नहीं: ब्राह्मण पंडित बहस में, जैन आचार्य सलाह में, और रेगिस्तान से सागर तक कारोबार करने वाले बनिये कर और व्यापार की फुसफुसाहट में।

panels.shot: close-up on Hemachandra in a dim library, manuscripts around him
panels.action: Hemachandra, lean and composed, sits in a quiet chamber of stacked palm-leaf bundles, stylus in hand, pausing thoughtfully over an open manuscript.

dialogue.text: Among them rises Hemachandra, a Jain monk whose mind ranges over grammar, ethics, and politics; in later memory, he becomes the king’s most trusted teacher.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं के बीच उभरते हैं हेमचंद्र, जैन मुनि जिनका मन व्याकरण, नीति और राजकाज तक दौड़ता है; आगे चलकर वे राजा के सबसे विश्वसनीय गुरु बन जाते हैं।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot, both seated on a low platform, lamp between them
panels.action: In a modest palace chamber lit by a single oil lamp, Kumarapala sits cross-legged opposite Hemachandra, who gently gestures toward a palm-leaf text between them.

dialogue.text: Jain texts like Somaprabha’s Kumarapala-Pratibodha picture long evenings of counsel, where the monk teaches the king how rule itself can be an act of restraint.

i18n.hi: सोमप्रभ के ‘कुमारपाल-प्रतिबोध’ जैसे जैन ग्रंथ लंबी सलाह की शामें दिखाते हैं, जहाँ मुनि सिखाते हैं कि खुद राज करना भी संयम का साधन हो सकता है।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot of a royal procession approaching hills
panels.action: A royal procession with elephants and horsemen climbs a rocky track toward the hills of Taranga, Kumarapala riding at the front, while Hemachandra walks calmly beside, staff in hand.

dialogue.text: Out of this closeness, Jain tradition says, grew great works: in 1161, atop the hills of Taranga, Kumarapala sponsors the Ajitanatha temple, a jewel of stone and faith.

i18n.hi: इसी नज़दीकी से, जैन परंपरा कहती है, बड़े कर्म जन्म लेते हैं: ११६१ में तारंगा की पहाड़ियों पर कुमारपाल अजीतनाथ मंदिर खड़ाकर पत्थर और आस्था का रत्न रचते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Taranga Ajitanatha temple under construction
panels.action: Stonecutters, artisans, and monks move across the half-built Ajitanatha temple at Taranga, as Kumarapala watches from a platform and Hemachandra points out details of the rising shikhara.

dialogue.text: Here, masons and monks work side by side, carving a Jain image into the land, while the king’s treasury turns quarry dust into domes and halls for Ajitanatha.

i18n.hi: यहाँ राज मिस्त्री और मुनि साथ-साथ, ज़मीन पर जैन मूर्ति उकेरते हैं, जबकि राजकोष खदान की धूल को अजीतनाथ के लिए गुंबद और मंडपों में बदल देता है।

panels.shot: close-up on a palm-leaf manuscript of Arhanniti beside royal emblems
panels.action: On a low desk, a neatly inscribed palm-leaf manuscript of Hemachandra’s Arhanniti lies open beside a small royal seal and a sheathed sword, Hemachandra’s hand resting lightly near the text.

dialogue.text: Hemachandra’s Arhanniti is a rare Jain treatise on statecraft, weaving non-violence and self-control into advice on taxes, courts, and the duties of a king surrounded by arms.

i18n.hi: हेमचंद्र की ‘अर्हन्नीति’ राज्य-नीति पर दुर्लभ जैन ग्रंथ है, जो अहिंसा और आत्मसंयम को कर, अदालत और हथियारों से घिरे राजा के कर्तव्यों की सलाह में पिरोता है।

panels.shot: medium shot in council, courtiers divided in subtle factions
panels.action: In the council hall, Kumarapala listens, brows knit, as Hemachandra speaks calmly on one side and Brahmin counselors on the other exchange quiet glances, each camp wary yet composed.

dialogue.text: Court debates sharpen: Jain advisors urge limits on sacrifice and slaughter, Brahmin priests guard ancient rites, and the king must balance devotion with the many ties of his realm.

i18n.hi: दरबारी बहसें तेज़ होती हैं: जैन सलाहकार बलि और वध पर लगाम चाहते हैं, ब्राह्मण पुजारी पुरानी विधि बचाते हैं, और राजा को भक्ति और रिश्तों की रस्सी पर संतुलन रखना पड़ता है।

panels.shot: close-up on Kumarapala’s face, half-lit, reflecting inner conflict
panels.action: Kumarapala’s face fills the frame, one side in lamplight and the other in shadow, his eyes lowered in thought as distant temple bells seem to echo on the edge of hearing.

dialogue.text: Jain narratives remember a turning point: under Hemachandra’s influence, they say, Kumarapala renounces meat, curbs animal sacrifice, and leans his heart toward ahimsa.

i18n.hi: जैन कथाएँ मोड़ का ज़िक्र करती हैं: हेमचंद्र के असर में, वे कहते हैं, कुमारपाल मांस छोड़ते हैं, पशु बलि घटाते हैं, और दिल को अहिंसा की तरफ़ झुकाते हैं।

panels.shot: split-detail shot: one side showing imagined bans, other side a blank stone
panels.action: On one side, an imagined scene shows royal officers stopping an animal sacrifice at a village, while on the other, a close-up of a bare stone wall hints at the absence of such orders in inscriptions.

dialogue.text: Yet, no inscription so far records a formal ahimsa edict; historians see these Jain stories as powerful community memory, not as decrees carved in stone.

i18n.hi: पर अब तक कोई शिलालेख साफ़-साफ़ अहिंसा का फरमान नहीं दिखाता; इतिहासकार इन जैन कहानियों को समुदाय की ताकतवर याद मानते हैं, पत्थर पर खुदा हुक्म नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Somnath coast with temple and waves
panels.action: Waves crash against the rocky shore at Somnath as artisans and laborers move around a temple complex, and Kumarapala supervises works amid banners bearing Shaiva symbols.

dialogue.text: Meanwhile, the Veraval inscription near Somnath still names him a devoted Shaiva, recalling his patronage of that shrine even as Jain stories claim him as their exemplar king.

i18n.hi: उधर, सोमनाथ के पास वेरावल का शिलालेख अभी भी उन्हें भक्त शिवभक्त राजा कहता है, उस मंदिर पर उनके वरदहस्त को याद करता है, जबकि जैन कथाएँ उन्हें अपना आदर्श नरेश मानती हैं।

panels.shot: scholarly montage, modern historian examining inscriptions and manuscripts
panels.action: A modern scholar in a quiet archive studies an ink rubbing of an inscription and then a Jain manuscript, both laid out on a wooden table, candlelight throwing long shadows.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, scholars like John Cort place these pieces together—inscriptions praising a Shaiva king, Jain texts celebrating a near-Jain ruler—and ask what kind of devotion a 12th-century monarch could display.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद जॉन कॉर्ट जैसे विद्वान ये टुकड़े जोड़ते हैं—शैव राजा की प्रशंसा करते शिलालेख, और लगभग-जैन नरेश गाते जैन ग्रंथ—और पूछते हैं कि बारहवीं सदी का राजा कैसी भक्ति दिखा सकता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hemachandra teaching students in a Jain upashraya
panels.action: Hemachandra sits on a simple platform in a Jain upashraya, a circle of laymen and young monks around him, as he gestures outward, linking scriptural teaching to the affairs of kings.

dialogue.speaker: kumarapala_and_hemachandra
dialogue.text: “Rule yourself, then your kingdom,” Hemachandra is remembered as saying.

i18n.hi: “पहले खुद पर राज करो, फिर अपने राज्य पर,” ऐसा हेमचंद्र के मुँह से याद किया जाता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Patan’s temples and markets thriving together
panels.action: A bustling street in Patan shows a Jain temple, a Shaiva shrine, and market stalls side by side, as officials of different dress mingle, and Kumarapala rides past in a palanquin, observing quietly.

dialogue.text: Under Kumarapala, Jain institutions prosper; Shaiva temples still stand; merchants grow rich; and the court becomes a place where rival visions of righteousness must share the same road.

i18n.hi: कुमारपाल के समय जैन संस्थाएँ खिलती हैं; शैव मंदिर अब भी खड़े हैं; बनिये मालामाल; और दरबार ऐसा मंच बनता है जहाँ अलग-अलग धर्मधाराएँ एक ही राह बाँटती हैं।

panels.shot: subtle scene of the ageing king and monk walking in a courtyard
panels.action: In a quiet palace courtyard at sunset, an older Kumarapala walks slowly beside Hemachandra, both moving in companionable silence between colonnades and flowering trees.

dialogue.text: When the king and the monk fade from the scene, what remains is a pattern: a Shaiva ruler deeply marked by Jain ethics, and a Jain thinker who steps boldly into the language of power.

i18n.hi: जब राजा और मुनि दोनों मंच से उतर जाते हैं, जो बचता है वह एक नक्शा है: जैन नीति से गहराई तक रंगा शैव नरेश, और एक जैन चिंतक जो निडर होकर सत्ता की भाषा में उतरता है।

panels.shot: final reflective montage, overlaying Kumarapala’s figure with inscription and Jain temple silhouette
panels.action: Kumarapala’s calm profile is overlaid with the faint outline of a Jain temple and the traced letters of a stone inscription, all set against a darkened map of Gujarat.

dialogue.text: Kumarapala and Hemachandra remind us that honest history holds many truths at once: a king can bow to Shiva, fund Jain temples, hear a monk’s counsel—and leave us questions instead of a single, tidy tale.

i18n.hi: कुमारपाल और हेमचंद्र याद दिलाते हैं कि सच्चा इतिहास कई सच साथ रखता है: एक राजा शिव के आगे झुक सकता है, जैन मंदिरों को धन दे सकता है, मुनि की सुन सकता है—और हमारे लिए एक साफ़-सुथरी कहानी नहीं, कई सवाल छोड़ सकता है।

title_i18n.en: Kumarapala and the Question of Faith

subtitle_i18n.en: A king, a monk, and the many faces of faith in Gujarat
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक राजा, एक साधु, और गुजरात में कई चेहरों वाली आस्था
